chunks: Allah is sufficient, and how [is it] for the one whom Allah does not suffice?

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, when He created the creation, made among them four wretched ones: a man whom Allah does not suffice, a man whom His Messenger does not suffice, a man whom his Imam does not suffice, and a man whom his sacrifice (Qurban) does not suffice.

key_terms.لَا يَكْفِيهِ إِمَامُهُ: whom his Imam does not suffice
key_terms.لَا يَكْفِيهِ رَسُولُهُ: whom his Messenger does not suffice
key_terms.لَا يَكْفِيهِ قُرْبَانُهُ: whom his sacrifice does not suffice

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of wretched people mentioned in the hadith of Kifayah?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) classification of the wretched (*Aqibah al-Su*) based on the failure of divine sufficiency (*Kifayah*) at four hierarchical levels: Allah, the Prophet, the Imam, and the ritual sacrifice. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine of the Imam’s essential role as the guarantor of spiritual and worldly sufficiency, linking the concept of *Kifayah* directly to the chain of authority (*Silsilah*) from God to the Imams.
